Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 1:

(p-208) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat at-Talaq

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period (iddah), and count the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord﴾ – the verse.

It has been said regarding the occasion of its revelation that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Hafsah (may Allah be pleased with her), and so it was revealed. It has also been said otherwise. In any case, the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, not in the specificity of the occasion of revelation, as is well known.

Among what confirms this principle is that if we take into careful consideration the noble connection between the two surahs, the subject matter at the end of the preceding surah was children and wives, with their trials and enmity.

The allusion to treating what passes between spouses by way of spending and tolerance, as we pointed out earlier there, is that if their relationship is set right by that, then well and good. But if the relationship between them becomes impossible to mend and separation becomes inevitable, this surah came right after it to explain the sound method of separation in divorce, its legislation, and what follows from it regarding waiting periods, maintenance, and the like.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet﴾ is an address by way of calling to the Prophet ﷺ. His saying ﴿when you divorce﴾ is an address in the plural to the community in general. They said: the calling was to the Prophet ﷺ and the address was to the community, as an honouring of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and an obligation upon the community. It has also been said: the community was addressed in the person of the Messenger ﷺ, like the address to a group in the person of its leader.

The Shaykh – may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him – said: From this verse those who hold that the Messenger ﷺ is included in the generality of the address to the community have derived their evidence. End of quote.

The reality is that the address directed to the Prophet ﷺ is of three categories:

The first: the address may be directed to him ﷺ without him being included in it at all, and it is intended for the community without any disagreement. An example of this is His saying, exalted is He, concerning kindness to parents: ﴿If one of them or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them "uff" and do not scold them, but speak to them a noble word. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small."﴾ [al-Isra: 23-24] (p-209)

So all the forms of address here are directed to the Prophet ﷺ, and he is certainly not intended by them, since at the time of their revelation he had no parents, nor either of them, as is well known.

The second: that it is specific to him, with no one else entering along with him, certainly. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her – a privilege for you, not for the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50].

The third: that which includes him ﷺ and others, as is evidenced by this verse and by the beginning of the surah that follows it in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ [at-Tahrim: 1]. All of this is an address directed to him ﷺ.

Immediately after it comes: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you﴾, with an address to everyone: ﴿the dissolution of your oaths﴾ [at-Tahrim: 2]. This shows that the verse is included in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [at-Tahrim: 1], and this is by agreement.

The Shaykh – may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him – has clarified this question with the strongest evidence on it at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth…﴾, up to His saying: ﴿turning back to Him in repentance﴾ [ar-Rum: 30-31].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you divorce women﴾ – the verse – implies that all divorced women are divorced at their waiting period and that their waiting period is counted.

Al-ihsa' means counting, derived from al-hasa', meaning small pebbles, which the Arabs used for counting because of their illiteracy. Then He mentioned the waiting period for some divorced women but did not mention all of them, although among the divorced women are those who have no waiting period, namely those not yet consummated, and among the divorced women are those whose waiting period is not mentioned here.

Az-Zamakhshari said: there is neither generality nor specification here, because the word "women" (nisa') is a noun of class that applies to the whole and to the part. Here it has been applied to a part, namely those whose ruling is made clear by mention of their waiting period, and they are: those who have despaired of menstruation, the young girls, and those who are pregnant. The sum total of the waiting periods of women is summarised in the following: separation is either by life or by death, and the separated woman is either pregnant or not pregnant. The pregnant woman's waiting period ends with the delivery of her child, by consensus, and no weight is given to disagreement on this since the texts are sound. The non-pregnant woman's waiting period is four months and ten days (p-210) if she was consummated and if she was not. Separation during life is either with a consummated woman or with an unconsummated one. For the unconsummated there is no waiting period, by consensus. The consummated woman is either one of those who have menstrual periods (dhawat al-aqra'), so her waiting period is three qur', with disagreement over the meaning of qur'; or one who is not of those who have menstrual periods, such as the one who has despaired and the young girl, so her waiting period is three months.

The Shaykh – may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him – had already presented in the first volume, at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228], the classification of types of divorced women, consummated and unconsummated, and the types of waiting periods by qur', months, or pregnancy, and he explained the reconciliation of the general texts concerning all of this, which makes repetition here unnecessary.

* *

Note

All that has preceded concerning the waiting period applies specifically to free women. The matter of slave women remains.

As for slave women: pregnant ones are the same as free women in every respect. As for non-pregnant ones, the majority hold that their waiting period is half that of a free woman, except that since a menstrual cycle cannot be divided, their waiting period in terms of it is two menstrual cycles. This is by agreement of the four Imams.

As for those whose waiting period is in months, the majority hold that she observes a month and a half, while Malik differed and gave her three months. Thus Malik agreed with the majority regarding those with menstrual periods, and differed from the majority regarding those with months. Ibn Rushd erred along with Malik in his discussion of this question, when he said in Bidayat al-Mujtahid:

"The statement of Malik on this question has been inconsistent: he took neither by the text nor acted by analogy." He means that he did not follow the text regarding those with menstrual periods by giving them three qur', as he did regarding those in months, where he gave them three months by the text, and he did not act by analogy, i.e., he did not halve the months by analogy with menstruation. So his school became a blend between analogy in the case of those with menstrual periods and the text in the case of those in months, and in this he differed from the three other Imams.

In Ibn Rushd's view his statement was inconsistent, because he did not apply analogy consistently in both cases, nor did he give effect to the text in both. But the truth in disputed matters cannot be known except after understanding the viewpoint of the opponent, for he may be correct, and it may in fact be that the truth lies with another.

(p-211) On this very question al-Adawi indicated in his gloss that Malik's viewpoint is a return to the underlying purpose of the waiting period, which is the clearing of the womb, and a month and a half is not sufficient for the woman herself to inform about herself whether she is pregnant or not, so he completed for her the period that was prescribed.

As for the two menstrual cycles, in them there is clear evidence of the clearing of the womb. End of quote, in summary.

What al-Adawi said has a basis in the Shariah, for we find that the woman with menstrual periods in some cases observes her waiting period by one menstrual cycle, as the text states regarding the waiting period of one who has been released by khul', though there is disagreement on it. And we find that a slave woman's womb is established as clear by two menstrual cycles with certainty in another case, namely if she is a concubine of her owner and he wishes to sell her: he establishes her womb's clearing by one menstrual cycle, and the one who buys her establishes it by one menstrual cycle before touching her; then he has intercourse with her, secure from watering another's field with his water. So we know that in the two menstrual cycles there is clearing of the womb, and Malik relied on them and agreed with the majority.

As for the month and a half, it is not possible for a woman to ascertain pregnancy within them, because it is the first forty-day period, the stage of the drop of semen. From this it becomes clear that the truth lies with Malik, and that it is Ibn Rushd whose statement on Malik was inconsistent. We have included this note to explain the obligation of the seeker of knowledge when faced with disputed matters: the necessity of inquiring into the reason and the viewpoint of the opponent, and not hastening to reject, lest he be the one more deserving of rejection, and lest he not hasten to refute a statement whose author may be more deserving of being refuted. And success is from Allah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So divorce them at their waiting period﴾ – the commentators agree that the meaning is to begin their waiting period, and in this is the discussion of the sunni and bid'i divorce. Know that a pregnant woman and an unconsummated woman have no bid'i divorce in their case according to the majority, and a young girl is joined to them. Bid'i divorce is the combining of three in one instance, or divorcing during menstruation, or in a purity period in which he has had intercourse with her. According to Imam Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, one divides the pronouncements upon the young girl, one pronouncement in each month, and does not combine them. The discussion has been lengthy regarding the ruling on bid'i divorce: does it take effect and is it counted against the one who divorces, or not?

Its basis is the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and Umar informed the Prophet ﷺ of this, and he said to him ﷺ: "Command him, so let him take her back."

What the majority hold is that he counts that pronouncement, and whoever has opposed the Sunnah in it must (p-212) take her back, and act as the Prophet ﷺ commanded: "Let him keep her until she becomes pure, then if he wishes he may keep her, and if he wishes he may divorce her in a purity period in which he has not touched her." That is, so that she begins her waiting period, unless it is the third pronouncement or three together, as the majority hold.

Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about counting this pronouncement given during menstruation, and he said: His saying, "Let him take her back," indicates that it is counted, for there is no taking back except from a divorce.

Ibn Daqiq al-Id spoke at length on it in Ihkam al-Ahkam and elsewhere, more than there is need to recount, and its essence is what we have already presented. No one held that it is not counted except Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and a group of the Successors.

Abu Hayyan said: His saying, exalted is He, "So divorce them at their waiting period," in its unrestricted form indicates that divorce is counted, whether it is sunni or bid'i.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

Surat at-Talaq

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet﴾ – the verse. It is apparent that the address is specific to him ﷺ, while His saying: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ – the verse [at-Talaq: 1] requires otherwise.

The answer is what was previously established in detail in Surat ar-Rum: that the address specific to the Prophet ﷺ has a ruling that is general to the whole community.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness﴾.

Its apparent meaning is that retaining them in kindness applies when they have reached their term, even though when they have reached that limit they have already exited the waiting period (iddah) and the basis for taking them back has ended. But what is intended here is that they have drawn near their term without exceeding it, or are about to reach it in actuality. The rule (qa'idah) is that what is close to a thing is given its ruling, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed﴾ [al-Nahl: 98].

Similar to the verse is the hadith in his saying (ﷺ): "When one of you comes to the toilet, let him say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female unclean spirits (al-khubuth wal-khaba'ith)." Yet at the moment of entering, or during it, he is not permitted to say this; he says it when he is close to entering. So it is likewise here.

As for the woman divorced three times, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, examined it thoroughly at his saying, exalted is He: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229], in a treatment to which nothing can be added.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has set a measure for everything.﴾

After the command to count the 'iddah (the waiting period), and the fact that the 'iddahs are of different kinds, from menstrual cycles (quru') to months to the delivery of the pregnancy, and that the women observing 'iddah differ in their cycles and in the length of pregnancy, so that she may be at its beginning, middle or end, and all of this must be counted because of what follows from it of prohibition and permissibility, so she leaves the 'iddah of one and becomes lawful for the other (p-213).

As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And do not determine the marriage bond until the decreed term reaches its end﴾ [al-Baqarah: 235]. All of this is not possible except through counting.

Counting is only for a known measure. Accordingly, His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, Allah has set a measure for everything﴾ confirms all of this. Likewise, it contains a clear text that He, may He be exalted, has set for everything among things, whatever it may be, a measure which it does not exceed, neither by increase nor by decrease. And the word "thing" (shay') is the most general of all general terms.

Many verses have come indicating this generality, both general and specific. Among the general verses is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything with measure﴾ [al-Qamar: 49]. And His saying: ﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2]. And His saying: ﴿And everything with Him is by measure﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8]. And His saying ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 21] combined the general and the specific.

As for specific determination in a particular instance, His saying: ﴿And the sun runs to its stationary point. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. And the moon—We have determined for it stations until it returns like the old dry date stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 38–40].

It is a overwhelming power, perfect wisdom, compelling will, and dominant authority: the power of One whose command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.

The astronomers have said: the calculation of the courses of these orbits in their stations is as precise as hundreds of parts of a second, and if one part of a second differed, the order of the world would be disrupted and life would not be fit on the face of the earth. We witness the movement of night and day, their decrease and increase, and the seasons of the year, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And Allah determines the night and the day. He knows that you cannot count them﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20].

He, glorified and exalted, counts them. Likewise is the determination for the existence of man before and after his existence. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop He created him and determined him﴾ [‘Abasa: 18–19], that is: He determined his creation, his form and his kind, as He clarified by His saying: ﴿He bestows female [offspring] upon whom He wills and bestows male [offspring] upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females﴾ — to His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent﴾ [al-Shura: 49–50].

This too is among the signs of His power, by which He, glorified, refutes those who deny the existence of Allah and disbelieve in the Resurrection (p-214), as in its opening, His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Destroyed is man; how disbelieving is he! From what thing did He create him?﴾ [‘Abasa: 17–18].

Then He, may He be exalted, clarified that He created him from a drop of despised water, but Allah, may He be exalted, determined its capacity and its form until it became a proportioned creature, and made for him, while he was in his mother's womb, two eyes, and a tongue, and two lips—that is, and a nose and two ears and two hands and two feet, and every apparatus in him which has bewildered the wise in its craftsmanship and its order.

Then He, may He be exalted, determined his provisions upon the earth before his existence, on the day He created the earth, and made it a sign of His power, and reproached man for his disbelief: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed therein firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and determined therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 9–10].

And after the existence of the universe and the creation of man, He determined, in bringing into being, by sending down rain: ﴿Then let man look at his food, that We poured down the water in torrents, then We split the earth in splitting, and caused to grow therein grain and grapes﴾ [Fussilat: 24–28].

Then the pouring of this water was by measure, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We sent down from the sky water in measure﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18].

And His saying: ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills; indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 27], that is: in the measure that suits them; if He increased it, their condition would be corrupted, as in His saying before it: ﴿And if Allah extended provision for His servants, they would commit tyranny upon the earth, but He sends down in measure what He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 27]. And according to the measure of their benefit He sends down their provisions for them.

As He drew attention to this by His saying: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6–7].

This is a glimpse into the wisdom of the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Wise, who perfected everything He created, and who determined things before their existence, as in His saying: ﴿And He who determined and then guided﴾ [al-A'la: 3].

And as in the hadith of the pen and the writing of everything before its existence, with its time, its place and its quantity. The sign of power and the demonstration of incapacity is the power of the Creator and the incapacity of the created, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ [al-A'raf: 34].

And like His saying: ﴿And no one is granted long life, nor is anything reduced from his lifespan, except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11], that is: (p-215) it does not exceed it nor transgress it. Allah has challenged them in this by His saying: ﴿Then why, when [the soul] has reached the throat, and you at that time are looking on—and We are closer to him than you, but you do not see—why, if you are not to be recompensed, do you not return it, if you should be truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. "No!" Indeed they are to be recompensed, and they will not be able to return it.

Here it is said to the materialists (al-Dahriyyin) and the communists who do not acknowledge the existence of a chooser agent and a mighty, dominant Lord: indeed this universe, with its determinations and its systems, is a witnessing sign and a clear, just proof of the existence of Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿So glory be to He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83].

As it is also said to the believers: indeed what Allah has determined is executed, and what has been decreed for the servant will come to him, and what has not been decreed for him he will never reach. The scrolls have been folded and the pens have dried: ﴿So that you not despair over what has eluded you, nor exult over what He has given you﴾ [al-Hadid: 23].

And it is said once more: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created," and with Allah, exalted is He, is success.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾.

In it there is a general statement regarding the delivery of the burden, in whatever form it may be. The scholars have agreed that it applies whether the delivery is of a living child or a dead one. However, it is stipulated that the fetus must have already shown the form of a human being, not a lump of flesh (mudghah) nor a clinging clot (alaqah). Likewise, the term (ajal) is stated in general terms, whether for a woman who has been divorced or for a woman whose husband has died: the term of pregnant women ends with the delivery of the burden. The explanation of this has already been given in detail by our Shaykh, may the mercy of Allah the Exalted be upon us and upon him. Here there is the topic of the minimum and maximum period of pregnancy (aqall al-haml wa akthharihi), and its detailed treatment was also previously given by the Shaykh when commenting on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears﴾ up to the verse (13:8).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then if they breastfeed for you, give them their payment, and confer among yourselves with kindness.﴾

Exalted is He has specified the period of breastfeeding in His saying: ﴿And mothers suckle their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]

Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) made three months in addition to the two years, for the purpose of accustoming the infant to weaning, and this is in accordance with His saying: ﴿for whoever wishes to complete the nursing.﴾

So if weaning the infant before that is possible without harm to him, there is no objection. The father must give the wage for the period of nursing until weaning, whether the period is the legally prescribed one, as here, or the actual period before it. He is not obligated to pay for what exceeds the two years mentioned in the text of the verse. (p-216)

The phrase "with kindness" (bi-ma'ruf) indicates that custom (al-'urf) has a role in this matter, as it is an explicit reminder that neither parent should harm the other through the child, and that the dealings between the spouses after separation, in all matters, including breastfeeding in particular or otherwise, should be founded on kindness, forbearance and goodness, in fulfillment of the right of the previous companionship. And ﴿do not forget graciousness among yourselves.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how many a city rebelled against the command of its Lord﴾, and the rest of the verse.

The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, mentioned in his *Mudhakkirat al-Imla'* (his dictation notes) that *ka'ayyin* means *kam* (how many), and that it indicates a large number. He also mentioned its *i'rab* (grammatical analysis). The meaning is: many a city rebelled against the command of its Lord, that is, it became arrogant and transgressed. He had already explained its meaning in detail, with examples and evidence, at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So how many a city We destroyed while it was wrongdoing﴾ [al-Hajj: 45], in Surat "al-Hajj."

Among what he presented, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, and from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those cities—We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾ [al-Kahf: 59], is a clarification for the people of leadership and the men of politics (*siyasah*) that the destruction of the world comes through the corruption of religion, and that the security of cities and the tranquility of the world lie in preserving religion.

From here came the enjoining of what is good (*al-amr bil-ma'ruf*) and the forbidding of what is evil (*al-nahy 'an al-munkar*) among the common people, to preserve their religion and the safety of their worldly life. The Lawgiver (*al-Shari'*) assigned this duty to the whole nation, each according to his ability: by the hand, by the tongue, or by the heart. This last is "the weakest of faith." Yet even with its weakness, it maintains the continuing awareness of the presence of evil until he, or someone else, is able to change it.

God, Exalted is He, has clarified this concept by describing the condition of those whom He established in the land with His help, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is good, and forbid what is evil; and to God belongs the outcome of all matters﴾ [al-Hajj: 41].

Then He mentioned the nations that denied and transgressed: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, Lut, and the companions of Madyan.

Then He said: ﴿So how many a city We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so it lies in ruins upon its roofs, and [many] a well abandoned and a lofty palace﴾ [al-Hajj: 45].

The author said in (*Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected provision for him.﴾

The pronoun is singular in this verse in His saying "يُؤْمِن" (yu'min, "believes"), in His saying "يَعْمَلْ" (ya'mal, "does"), in His saying "يُدْخِلْهُ" (yudkhilhu, "He will admit him"), and in His saying "لَهُ" (lahu, "for him"). It is plural in His saying "خالِدِينَ" (khalidin, "abiding").

The answer: the singular is in view of the wording of "مَن" (man, "whoever"), and the plural is in view of its meaning. This is common in the Great Qur'an. In this noble verse there is a refutation of one who claimed that once the meaning has been observed, observing the wording afterward is not permissible, because in this verse He observed the meaning in His saying "خالِدِينَ", then observed the wording in His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly perfected provision for him.﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 65, verse 12:

(p-217) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾.

It has come in the explanation of the heavens that they are seven layers (ṭibāq), as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He who created seven heavens in layers﴾ [al-Mulk: 3].

The hadith on the Night Journey (isrā') explained that the distance between each heaven and the next is a journey of five hundred years. The word "heaven" (samā') has come both singular and plural. The singular is as in His saying: ﴿And the heaven and He who constructed it﴾ [al-Shams: 5], and His saying: ﴿He who made for you the earth a bed and the heaven a canopy﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22].

As for the earth, its word has come only in the singular, and its detail has not come as the detail of the heaven as seven layers. So scholars differed regarding the "likeness" (mithliyyah). It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is a complete likeness in number, layers and creation. It was said: in number and in regions (aqālīm) separated by seas. It was said: in number, as layers piled upon one another like the layers of an onion, for example. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already mentioned in the introduction that among the modes of explanation, if a matter is not found in the Book but is found in the Sunnah, it is explained by it, because it is revelation (waḥy). The Sunnah has indeed stated that the earth is seven earths, as in the hadith: "Whoever usurps a piece of land, or takes a span of land, will have it hung around his neck from seven earths." Agreed upon (Muttafaq ʿalayh).

And in the hadith of Moses, when he said: "O Lord, teach me something by which I may call upon You. He said: Say, there is no god but Allah. He said: O Lord, all the people say that. He said: O Moses, if the seven heavens and their inhabitants other than Me, and the seven earths were placed in one pan of a scale, and there is no god but Allah in the other pan, it would outweigh them, there is no god but Allah." Narrated by al-Nasāʾī.

These are sound hadiths which establish that the earths are seven. No detail has come regarding their manner or their form, so the number is established for us and nothing else is established, so we affirm it and leave the rest to the knowledge of Allah, may He be exalted.

Among what supports the establishment of the number in general terms is that the likeness of the earth to the heaven is mentioned only when the heaven is mentioned in general terms together with the number, and it is not mentioned when the heaven is detailed as layers, which indicates that the intended meaning of likeness is number. It was said: this does not conflict with the singular form of the word, since its plural is anomalous (shādh).

As Ibn Mālik said:

"And ʾarḍūn is anomalous, as is al-sinūn."

(p-218) Allah, may He be exalted, has also indicated that there are states of the earth and the heaven which creation does not know, in His saying: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]. They are still unable to know the manner of the creation of themselves beyond partial details. What is important from the context and the principal purpose is alerting creation to the greatness of Allah's power, in His saying: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 12].
